cards.front: Recall a key point about The Weimar Republic
cards.back: In October 1918, Germany was facing defeat in World War I. The Kaiser's government transformed into a parliamentary democracy to secure better peace terms. However, the revolution went further than intended when sailors mutinied at Kiel on 3 November 1918.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Weimar Republic
cards.back: The Weimar Constitution, approved on 11 August 1919, created the most democratic system Germany had ever known - but it contained crucial weaknesses that opponents exploited.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Weimar Republic
cards.back: Friedrich Ebert, leader of the SPD, became the first President of the Weimar Republic in February 1919. He governed using Article 48 136 times during his presidency (1919-1925), often to deal with political crises - setting a dangerous precedent for future use.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Weimar Republic
cards.back: In January 1919, the Communist Spartacist League (led by Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht) attempted to overthrow the Weimar government in Berlin. The government used the Freikorps (right-wing ex-soldiers) to crush the uprising. Luxemburg and Liebknecht were murdered on 15 January 1919.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Weimar Republic
cards.back: In March 1920, right-wing Freikorps units under Wolfgang Kapp attempted to seize control of Berlin. The army (Reichswehr) refused to fire on the Freikorps. The government survived only through a general strike called by trade unions, which paralysed Berlin and forced Kapp to flee.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Weimar Republic
cards.back: Between 1919 and 1922, right-wing extremists committed 354 political murders in Germany. Left-wing extremists committed 22. However, right-wing assassins received an average sentence of 4 months, while left-wing assassins received an average of 15 years. This showed the justice system was biased towards the right and against the Republic.

cards.front: What should you know about history exam tips — the weimar republic?
cards.back: 1. For The Weimar Republic, include specific factual detail: dates, names, events and statistics where relevant 2. For source questions, analyse provenance (who, when, why, audience) before using the content 3. In evaluation questions, discuss multiple factors and weigh their relative significance 4. Always link back to the question focus — don't just narrate what happened with The Weimar Republic 5. Use phrases like 'the most significant factor was... because...' to show analytical judgement
All men AND women over 20 could vote (previously only men over 25)
Seats in the Reichstag allocated proportionally to votes - every 60,000 votes = 1 seat
Elected by the people every 7 years; chose the Chancellor
The people could initiate referendums on key issues
